protections: The predictable server instance directory <temp_dir>/passenger.<maj>.<min>.<web_server_pid> may only be reused if the entry itself (not a symlink target) is a real directory owned by the current euid/egid with mode 0755. All later files (generation-*, control_process.pid, password files) are written by name under it, so this one ownership/type check protects all of them (ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:215-225, 262-284).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The reuse check added by the CVE-2014-1831 fix already verifies mode and owner, so the directory looks protected.
evidence: ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:216 getFileType(path) uses stat(), which follows symlinks (ext/common/Utils.cpp:123), so a symlink to a directory is classified FT_DIRECTORY
ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:266 verifyDirectoryPermissions uses stat(), not lstat(), so it checks mode and owner on the symlink target. Any root-owned 0755 directory passes lines 269 and 272
ext/common/agents/Watchdog/Main.cpp:589-594 the path is predictable from tempDir and web_server_pid

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The directory was verified just before, at initialize().
evidence: ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:73 the generation path is built by string concatenation from the instance path, so every later operation re-resolves the name. If that name is a symlink an attacker owns, it can be retargeted after the check at :266 (the time window between the two filesystem operations)
ext/common/Utils.cpp:618-620 makeDirTree returns early if the generation path already exists (stat follows symlinks), and it never checks owner or mode
ext/common/Utils.cpp:158 createFile opens by path with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC and without O_NOFOLLOW when overwrite is true

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The file lives inside the root-owned server instance directory, so only root could have planted a link there.
evidence: ext/nginx/ngx_http_passenger_module.c:216 create_file uses fopen("w"), which follows a symlink and truncates, with no O_EXCL
ext/nginx/ngx_http_passenger_module.c:328 chown() by path to the worker uid follows a symlink at control_process.pid
ext/nginx/ngx_http_passenger_module.c:135 save_master_process_pid reopens it with fopen("w") after the privilege drop
This is the advisory's named sink (control_process.pid). It is exploitable only when the instance directory guard (T1/T2) fails

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The comment says it exists only to make unit tests pass. Production loaders override it with generation_dir.
evidence: lib/phusion_passenger/utils/tmpdir.rb:47 a second implementation of the same predictable /tmp/passenger.1.0.<pid> name
lib/phusion_passenger/utils/tmpdir.rb:51 File.exist? follows symlinks, and the code reuses any existing entry with no owner or mode check
helper-scripts/rack-loader.rb:80, helper-scripts/rack-preloader.rb:84, helper-scripts/classic-rails-loader.rb:74 production paths set passenger_tmpdir explicitly, so this fallback is mostly test-only

traps.reason_to_dismiss: In a sticky /tmp, an attacker cannot rename or replace a directory root has just created, so chmod/chown by path is safe there.
evidence: ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:242 chmod() and :250 chown() run by path after mkdir() at :236 rather than through a directory fd. This is only exploitable when passenger_temp_dir/PASSENGER_TEMP_DIR points to a non-sticky, shared-writable directory (ext/common/Utils.cpp:598-606, ext/apache2/Configuration.cpp:258)

masking: T3 (control_process.pid symlink-follow) is reachable only while T1/T2 leave the instance directory attacker-controllable. Fixing T1 with lstat plus an owner check makes T3 unexploitable in a sticky /tmp.

conflicts.what: Rejecting any pre-existing instance directory, as an over-hardened alternative to lstat-verify, breaks the legitimate reuse path. That path exists because the same web-server PID survives Passenger upgrades and graceful reloads (ext/common/agents/Watchdog/Main.cpp:584-588; ServerInstanceDir.h:220-221, 273-280). The fix must still accept a real, own-uid, 0755 directory.

fairness_risks: Reuse of an existing, correctly owned 0755 server instance directory must keep working (ServerInstanceDir.h:220-221; Watchdog/Main.cpp:584-588). A test that refuses all pre-existing directories would contradict this.

Admins may set passenger_temp_dir to a path whose parent components are symlinks (for example /tmp -> /private/tmp on macOS). A fix that refuses symlinks anywhere in the path, rather than only at the final instance-dir component, breaks a legitimate setup (ext/common/Utils.cpp:598-606, ext/apache2/Configuration.cpp:258).

control_process.pid must stay writable by the nginx worker uid after the privilege drop (ngx_http_passenger_module.c:315-333). Creating it 0600 root-owned with O_EXCL and no chown would break save_master_process_pid.

design.why: Only one independent group with real security weight exists: T1/T2/T3, all closed by an lstat-based type/owner check on the instance directory. T4 is a test-only second implementation whose own comment gives a strong reason to dismiss it. T5 is exploitable only under a non-default, non-sticky temp_dir. Neither is a convincing independent trap for hidden behavioural tests, and there is no genuine mimo-type (coupled value or how-type) trap. If forced, T1 plus T3 (as a separate O_NOFOLLOW/O_EXCL fix site) plus T4 gives the most distinct reasons to dismiss. T3 is masked by T1, though, so the design is effectively one judgement plus defence-in-depth. It is below the 3-5 independent-trap bar.

unverified: The exact contents of the B fix 94428057c602 were not viewed (no git access in this run). That it switches stat to lstat in ServerInstanceDir and/or adds O_NOFOLLOW to the control_process.pid creation is inferred from the advisory text (symlink attack on control_process.pid / generation-*) and the pinned code.

That lines ServerInstanceDir.h:215-284 (createDirectory/verifyDirectoryPermissions) were introduced by the A fix 34b1087870c2 is inferred from the 1831 advisory and the comment at :257-261. The A diff was not viewed.

lib/phusion_passenger/admin_tools/server_instance.rb:122-126 runs FileUtils.chmod_R/rm_rf on stale /tmp/passenger.* entries, possibly as root. Whether this follows attacker-planted symlinks depends on the Ruby FileUtils version (lchmod handling), so it was not recorded as a trap.

Whether the Apache module writes control_process.pid or any file directly under the instance directory by name was not traced beyond ext/apache2/Hooks.cpp:1312-1325, which write under the generation directory.
